subject: NeuralGrid: k6 rehearsal — traffic matrix, streaming concurrency & IP allowlist
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@neuralgrid.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: NeuralGrid k6 rehearsal — draft traffic matrix and allowlist ask

Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps so we can get your customer-led rehearsal scheduled.

Key SLOs you confirmed
- 95th pctl latency target: <= 250ms (text-only generation, 1k token context)
- Sustained throughput target: 450 reqs/sec (burst to 900 for 3m)
- Streaming concurrency: up to 60 concurrent streaming sessions (clients maintain SSE)

What we need from your side to proceed
1) IP allowlist for the test window — please paste CIDR(s) into ip_allowlist_submission.txt and confirm ownership for firewall rules.
2) Test accounts / API keys: a non-prod API key or temporary service token scoped for rehearsal (token TTL >= 4h).
3) Traffic matrix: sample mix of endpoints (chat/generate/embedding) + ratio. I attached a draft (neuralgrid_traffic_matrix.csv) — please edit if the client workload differs.
4) Preferred test window (2-hour slot, Mon–Fri, PDT).

Technical notes for the rehearsal (k6 preferred)
- We'll run a k6 script (attached sample_k6_script.js) that models concurrent streaming by establishing long-lived connections and ramping HTTP POSTs for non-streaming paths.
- KV cache warmup: include an initial ramp of 5 minutes at 25% load to prime embeddings and prefix cache.
- Metrics we'll collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies, token/sec, 429/503 counts, active streams over time.

Proposed immediate actions
- You: confirm IP CIDRs + provide test token by Mon 09:00 PDT
- Us (Markus + DevOps on-call): schedule rehearsal and share k6 runner details + public origin IPs for allowlist

Attachments: sample_k6_script.js (k6 scenarios), neuralgrid_traffic_matrix.csv (editable), ip_allowlist_submission.txt (template), runbook-rehearsal-checklist.pdf

Thanks — I’ll sync with Monica and Soojin on ops sequencing once you confirm the window.

—
Markus Klein
Sales Lead, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Samir Patel <samir@neuralgrid.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: NeuralGrid DevOps <devops@neuralgrid.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 20:49:00 +0000
Subject: Re: NeuralGrid k6 rehearsal — draft traffic matrix and allowlist ask

Hi Markus — this is perfect, thanks for the clear checklist. A few clarifications and answers below.

1) IPs: attaching the CIDRs we control (see ip_allowlist_submission.txt). We can also add your runner IPs if you provide them; otherwise we will open a short temporary hole for your known runner pool.
2) Token: I created a scoped rehearsal token (rehearsal-ng-2026) with 8h TTL and limited to the staging project. I’ll send credentials to the secure channel (ops slack) — will not put secrets in email.
3) Traffic mix tweaks: our real workload is 65% streaming chat (partial updates), 25% small generate (1–2 turns), 10% embedding lookups. I updated neuralgrid_traffic_matrix.csv accordingly.
4) Concurrency: we can hit 60 concurrent streams but expect client-side backpressure — worth observing token/segment throughput.

Preferred window: Tue 2026-06-22, 16:00–18:00 PDT. That gives our internal QA a chance to sanity-check scripts on Monday.

A couple of asks for your ops team:
- Please confirm how streaming sessions map to k6 VUs in your script (we run clients from our side too).
- Will Redwood provide a public test origin IP list for the allowlist before Tue morning?

Samir
VP Engineering
NeuralGrid
samir@neuralgrid.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: NeuralGrid k6 rehearsal — draft traffic matrix and allowlist ask

Thanks — looping in ops details. Soojin, quick ops checklist and tentative plan:

- Runner IP list: we’ll use the standard k6 runner pool. Current public egress for the pool (to provide to NeuralGrid): 34.83.120.12/32, 34.83.120.13/32, 34.83.120.14/32. I’ll verify with infra and push final list by Mon 08:00 PDT.
- k6 mapping for streaming: the attached sample_k6_script.js models streaming as dedicated VUs that open an SSE/WS connection and emit events; we also have a variant to proxy real client frames if they want identical framing.
- Metrics and dashboards: I created a provisional Grafana board (INF-1207) that captures token throughput, active stream count, and error budget burn. Add to related_links.
- Failover policy: if p95 breach > 30% over target for >5m, we will automatically scale to a warmer pool and notify both sides.

I’ll schedule the runner and post the confirmed IPs. Markus — can you send the HubSpot deal link and the rehearsal runbook to Sam in one secure share so we have the documentation trail?

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@neuralgrid.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 14:43:00 +0000
Subject: Re: NeuralGrid k6 rehearsal — draft traffic matrix and allowlist ask

Samir — great, thank you for the quick turnaround and the updated traffic mix. Confirming next steps and owners: 

- NeuralGrid: finalize CIDRs in ip_allowlist_submission.txt and share secure token in ops Slack (owner: Samir) — due Mon 08:00 PDT.
- Redwood Ops (Soojin): publish final runner IPs in this thread and to Samir via Ops Slack — due Mon 08:00 PDT.
- Redwood (Monica): prepare Grafana links and attach the rehearsal runbook PDF to the Drive folder.
- Redwood (Markus): schedule k6 slot for Tue 16:00–18:00 PDT and send meeting invite with runbook + HubSpot link.

I’ve added the HubSpot deal and runbook links to related_links in the thread metadata and uploaded the revised traffic matrix and the sample script to the Drive folder. I’ll also attach a condensed checklist to the calendar invite.

If anything changes on your side (token, window), please let us know by Mon 10:00 PDT so we can rebook. Otherwise we’ll consider this locked and proceed. Looking forward to the rehearsal — we’ll capture latency/throughput baselines and post a joint retrospective with action items.

—
Markus Klein
Sales Lead, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
